info.bio: A Flock of Seagulls es un grupo musical británico de estilo pop electrónico, derivado del New Wave de los años 80. En sus orígenes, la banda estaba formada por los hermanos Mike (sintetizadores, voz cantante) y Ali Score (batería), Frank Maudsley (bajo) y Paul Reynolds (guitarra). Su lanzamiento al estrellato internacional vino de la mano de la cadena de televisión musical MTV, con el video musical I Ran (So far away) (1982), canción que identifica perfectamente el estilo musical y estético de la banda.

scenes.name: Segunda invasión británica y MTV
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1982 el new pop deja de ser un sueño de periodistas: «Don't You Want Me», «Tainted Love» y «The Look of Love» anuncian una nueva invasión, y en 1983 la segunda camada (Duran Duran, Culture Club, Wham!, Eurythmics, Thompson Twins) conquista Estados Unidos gracias a MTV, canal ideado por Michael Nesmith que, sin vídeos americanos, dependía de los británicos, más videogénicos y cultivados en el estilo («I want my MTV»). A Flock of Seagulls, Altered Images («Happy Birthday»), Simple Minds («Promised You a Miracle», New Gold Dream), Haircut 100, Kajagoogoo; Bowie se broncea con «Let's Dance». El new pop reexporta música negra (Chic, P-Funk, Quincy Jones) a la América blanca. En el Reino Unido, 1983 se vive en cambio como un año infausto: reelección de Thatcher, «Kill Ugly Pop» en las paredes y la vuelta de la conciencia social.

podcast.title: Band Members as Hairdressers
podcast.body: Two members of A Flock of Seagulls had prior experience as hairdressers, a detail often cited in connection with the band's distinctive and often elaborate hairstyles. "Now there were two hairdressers in the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First British Technopop Billboard Top Ten Hit
podcast.body: A Flock of Seagulls achieved a significant milestone by being the first British Technopop band to break into the top ten of the Billboard singles chart, likely during the winter of 1981-82. This success was attributed not only to the song itself but also heavily to the extensive MTV play of its video and singer Mike Score's distinctive swoopy haircut. "As far as anyone can tell, this song was the first hit by a British Technopop band to reach the top ten of the Billboard singles chart. The song is fine, but it was MTV play of the video and singer Mike Scors' swoopy haircut that really made that happen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Iconic New Wave Hairstyle
podcast.body: The singer of A Flock of Seagulls is frequently the first individual recalled when discussing 1980s New Wave hairstyles, underscoring the profound impact of his visual presentation on the genre's aesthetic. "In fact, when you talk about new wave hairstyles from the 1980s, the first guy who inevitably comes to mind is the dude from a flock of seagulls."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Infamous Haircut of the 1980s
podcast.body: Frontman Mike Score had "probably the most infamous haircut of the entire 1980s." "And a Liverpool quartet whose frontman, Mike Skore, had probably the most infamous haircut of the entire 1980s."

podcast.title: MTV's Profound US Chart Impact
podcast.body: A Flock of Seagulls provided clear evidence of MTV's significant impact in the US, as they were "bigger in America than they ever were in the UK." Jonathan Bernstein, co-author of *Matt World*, noted that in the UK, they were seen as a "joke act," while American co-author Laurie Medjuski praised their videos, especially "I Ran," for being "full on resplendent technicolor." "A flock of Seagulls offered evidence of MTV's profound U.S. chart impact. They were bigger in America than they ever were in the UK."

podcast.title: Mike Score's Signature Haircut
podcast.body: Mike Score, the singer of A Flock of Seagulls, was recognized for his unique "goofy swoopy in your face haircut," which became a defining image for the band and a memorable new wave style. "And who could forget Mike Scorch's goofy swoopy in your face haircut?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Telegenic New Wave Band
podcast.body: Flock of Seagulls was highlighted as one of the "Telegenic New Wave bands" that achieved stardom with the advent of music videos on MTV (1981) and MuchMusic (1983). Their visual appeal played a significant role in showcasing music in a new light during this era. "And the stars of the show were the Telegenic New Wave bands like Flocke Seagulls and the Eridmix, and of course Durand Durand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: New Romantic Origin
xref.body: Duran Duran originated from the New Romantics scene, which began as a fashion movement in the UK in the late 1970s before adherents started creating music. Their unique style, blending punk, glam rock, and romantic period fashion, was central to the movement. "this was the origin of such groups as Durand Ran, Culture Club, Spandovalet, and a flock of Seagulls."
